interaction.prompt: The other team is packed into a neutral zone trap. You have the puck at the red line. Tap your best option.

feedback.right: The trap collapses toward the puck and leaves the far side thin. Your weak-side winger is stretching into that soft ice with room to carry it in with speed.
feedback.wrong: The centre and strong-side wing are both standing in ice the trap is built to protect — a pass there gets picked off before it arrives. The weak-side winger is the one lane the trap left open. Find the far side.

tip: A trap squeezes the puck side hard on purpose. The read is never through the middle of the wall — it's around it.
why: A neutral zone trap sacrifices the far side to overload pressure on the puck. Scanning across the whole width finds the soft ice the trap gave up, instead of forcing a pass into the numbers it stacked.
